相关性: 该论文将机器学习（随机森林）集成到球体融合过程的自动化监测中，直接支持基于球体的生物打印工作流中的后处理监测与分析。
边界: This paper does not involve AI-driven control of the bioprinting process itself, nor does it address printing path planning, bioink formulation, or real-time feedback control.
动机· 开发自动平台以量化监测球体融合动力学
方法· 随机森林半自动选择双球体对，自动分割提取形态特征并拟合动力学模型
结果· 平台准确提取特征并发现软骨成熟度增加会降低融合速率

English summary & terms
Motivation· To develop an automated platform for quantitative, high-throughput monitoring of spheroid fusion kinetics to replace manual analysis.
Method· A random forest classifier semi-automatically selects doublet candidates, followed by automatic segmentation and morphological feature extraction (area, roundness, contact length, intersphere angle) from time-lapse images, and exponential modeling of roundness over time.
Result· The platform achieved high accuracy in feature extraction (relative errors <5%) and revealed that increased chondrogenic maturation correlates with decreased fusion rate.
Validation· Experimental validation using spheroids from two cell pools at four stages of chondrogenic maturation (days 1, 7, 14, 21) with quantitative comparison to manual measurements.

Motivation· To investigate the influence of 3D-printed porous titanium alloy scaffold geometry on bone regeneration capability.
Method· Two unit structures (hollow hexagonal and triangular prisms) were fabricated by selective laser melting, characterized for morphology and mechanical properties, and evaluated through in vitro cell studies and in vivo animal implantation.

English summary & terms
Motivation· To mitigate stress shielding in hip implants caused by elastic modulus mismatch using a parametric design of gradient porous structure.
Method· A parametric design methodology combining Kriging surrogate modeling and response surface optimization is applied to determine the dimensions of each segment of the porous structure to achieve a gradient elastic modulus.
Result· The optimized gradient porous implant increased the femoral surface strain by 17.1% on average, effectively reducing the stress-shielding effect.
Validation· Experimental mechanical testing on a femur model validated the strain improvement.

English summary & terms
Motivation· To improve the osseointegration capacity of 3D-printed porous Ti6Al4V implants through a customized UV photofunctionalization surface treatment.
Method· An omnidirectional UV radiator was designed for uniform surface treatment of porous implants, and its effects were evaluated through in vitro cytocompatibility tests and in vivo rabbit condyle defect models.
Result· UV treatment significantly enhanced hydrophilicity, alkaline phosphatase activity, and in vivo osseointegration metrics (bone ingrowth, bone-implant contact ratio) while preserving original mechanical properties.
Validation· The study combined in vitro cell assays (cytocompatibility, ALP activity) and an in vivo animal model (rabbit condyle defect) to demonstrate osseointegration improvement.

Motivation· To demonstrate the credibility of a patient-specific finite element model of a lumbar spine segment with metastatic lesions for predicting vertebral surface displacements under physiological loading.

Validation· Experimental validation using cadaveric spine with Digital Image Correlation under combined compression-flexion loading.

English summary & terms
Motivation· To address the challenge of rapid vascularization in large engineered tissue constructs by developing a bioink that supports both complex architecture and microcapillary formation.
Method· Gelatin-norbornene (Gel-NOR) bioink was characterized for its tunable physico-mechanical properties and compatibility with extrusion and lithography-based bioprinting, and co-cultures of human stromal and endothelial cells were used to assess self-assembly of microcapillaries.
Result· Gel-NOR constructs with self-assembled microcapillaries were successfully fabricated, and the interplay between channel size, cell type, and structural changes was observed, with cross-signaling potentially causing lumen reduction.
Validation· In vitro cell experiments validated the bioink's ability to support microcapillary formation and its printability with defined physical architectures.

Validation· Experimental wear, hardness, and density measurements confirmed the predicted optimal parameter set.

结果· 搅拌摩擦焊具有最高抗拉强度，激光焊保持了较好的延展性，所有方法均导致马氏体相变。

English summary & terms
Motivation· To compare the influence of heat-affected zone on microstructure and mechanical properties across different welding methods for Ti-6Al-4V alloy.
Method· Tensile testing, hardness mapping, and microstructural analysis were performed on TIG, laser, friction stir, and SLM hybrid welded Ti-6Al-4V samples.
Result· Friction stir welding yielded the highest ultimate tensile strength, while laser welding retained the most ductility; all welding methods induced martensitic transformation and reduced ductility.
Validation· Experimental validation through tensile tests, hardness profiles, and microstructure characterization.

Method· Implant surfaces with micron/submicron roughness and added coarse cavities were placed in rabbit femoral condyles for 2 and 8 weeks, with analysis of bone-to-implant contact, bone volume density, and removal torque.

Motivation· To investigate how titanium implant surface roughness influences bone cell response for improving osseointegration.
Method· Human MG-63 osteoblast-like cells were cultured on smooth (solid titanium, PEEK) and rough (plasma-sprayed titanium) surfaces, with morphology and proliferation assessed via SEM, immunofluorescence, and WST-1 assay.

Validation· In vitro cell assays including Live/Dead, WST-1, and focal adhesion staining.

English summary & terms
Motivation· To evaluate whether laser-ablated surfaces improve osseointegration compared to machined surfaces in long-term bone healing.
Method· Commercially available titanium implants with laser-ablated or machined surfaces were implanted in sheep frontal bone; after five months, biopsies were analyzed by histology, histomorphometry, SEM, and Raman spectroscopy.
Result· Both implant types showed high bone-implant contact (67-71%) and mature lamellar bone, indicating comparable osseointegration.
Validation· The study used an in vivo sheep skull model with multi-modal post-mortem characterization.

Motivation· To compare the osseointegration performance of porous titanium alloys versus hydroxyapatite-coated titanium at the bone-implant interface.
Method· Sintered bionic trabecular porous titanium, 3D-printed porous titanium, and HA-coated titanium acetabular cups were fabricated and implanted in beagle dogs, followed by imaging and histomorphological analysis at 1, 3, and 6 months.

Motivation· To address insufficient osteogenesis in bone defect repair by combining a 3D-printed titanium scaffold with sequential release of growth factors.
Method· VEGF/BMP-2 shell-core microspheres were loaded onto a 3D-printed porous titanium alloy scaffold via gelatin coating to create a sustained-release system.

Validation· In vitro cell assays and in vivo rabbit femoral defect model with micro-CT, histology, and fluorescence labeling.

Motivation· To address the challenges of osseointegration and high shear forces in pelvic reconstruction after hemipelvectomy.
Method· Four pelvis models were constructed for finite element analysis under 500 N and 2000 N loads, with retrospective clinical outcomes from four patients.

Validation· Simulation-based biomechanical analysis supported by a retrospective clinical study with a mean follow-up of 16.6 months.

English summary & terms
Motivation· To compare mid-term clinical and radiographic outcomes of short versus conventional cementless femoral stems in patients with bilateral osteonecrosis of the femoral head.
Method· A retrospective study of 35 patients who received a short stem on one hip and a conventional stem on the other, evaluated with Harris Hip Score, thigh pain, patient perception, and X-ray analysis.
Result· The short stem group showed less thigh pain, more natural joint feeling, and higher patient preference, with evidence of better proximal load transfer and slightly lower stress shielding grade.
Validation· Clinical assessment and radiographic evaluation of osseointegration and stress shielding at mean 75-month follow-up.

Method· Process parameters were optimized to achieve 99.37% relative density, and the effects of density and heat treatment (solution and aging) on conductivity were systematically analyzed.

Validation· Validation was performed through density measurement and electrical conductivity testing, with systematic analysis of heat treatment mechanisms.

English summary & terms
Motivation· To compare the longitudinal stability of mandibular implants with Morse taper and external hexagon connections under immediate functional loading.
Method· Nine patients each received four mandibular implants with two Morse taper on left and two external hexagon on right; implant stability quotient (ISQ) was measured via resonance frequency analysis at multiple time points.
Result· Both connection types achieved reliable osseointegration (ISQ ≥ 67); only initial stability differed significantly, with external hexagon distal implants showing higher stability.
Validation· Clinical follow-up at 3 months, 6 months, and 2 years post-surgery using ISQ measurements.

Method· Cylindrical CMPC scaffolds post-treated with diammonium hydrogen phosphate (alkaline) or phosphoric acid (acid) were implanted into rabbit femoral condyles and evaluated via clinical, X-ray, μCT, histological, SEM, and EDX analysis up to 24 weeks.

Motivation· To evaluate facial-palatal ridge dimensional changes following dual-zone immediate implant placement versus socket-shield technique in the maxilla.

Validation· Clinical follow-up with intraoral measurements referenced to contralateral tooth sites.

English summary & terms
Motivation· To evaluate the clinical and functional outcomes of uncemented total hip arthroplasty in patients with avascular necrosis of the femoral head.
Method· A prospective study was conducted on 50 patients with stage III-IV avascular necrosis who underwent uncemented total hip arthroplasty; outcomes were assessed using the Harris hip score.
Result· The mean Harris hip score improved from 33.27 preoperatively to 91.60 postoperatively, with excellent results in 44 patients and good results in 6 patients.
Validation· Clinical follow-up and Harris hip score evaluation were used to assess the outcomes.

English summary & terms
Motivation· To investigate whether resonance frequency analysis reliably assesses primary stability of dental implants lacking apical contact.
Method· Eighty bone-level implants were placed into polyurethane blocks without apical contact, and RFA measurements were taken along transverse and longitudinal axes by two independent researchers.
Result· The 4 mm coronal contact group showed significantly lower stability, while fully placed implants did not exhibit the highest stability among apically contactless groups.
Validation· Validation was performed using polyurethane test blocks and interobserver reliability analysis with ICC values ranging from moderate to excellent.

Motivation· To investigate the histological and histomorphometric effects of intermittent parathyroid hormone administration on osseointegration in a glucocorticoid-induced osteoporotic rabbit model.
Method· Dental implants were inserted into the femoral epiphyses of osteoporotic rabbits after different PTH administration durations, and torque removal, bone-implant contact, and micro-CT analyses were performed.
Result· Continuous PTH administration for 8 weeks significantly improved removal torque and bone-implant contact ratio compared to shorter administration or control.
Validation· Validation was performed through in vivo animal experiments using mechanical removal torque testing, micro-computed tomography, and histomorphometric analysis.

Motivation· To evaluate the wear and performance of tripolar hip prostheses in high-demand patients over long-term implantation.
Method· Twenty-four retrieved tripolar prostheses were analyzed for volumetric wear, range of motion, and mechanical function after a mean of 14 years in vivo.

Validation· Validation was performed through clinical retrieval analysis and radiographic assessment.

English summary & terms
Motivation· The literature is conflicting on whether high hip center reconstruction is ideal for severe DDH; this study compares mid-term outcomes of HHC versus anatomical hip center in Crowe types II and III.
Method· A retrospective review of 57 primary THA patients was conducted, dividing them into anatomical (AHC) and high hip center (HHC) groups, with clinical Harris Hip Scores and radiographic assessment at mean 40-month follow-up.
Result· No significant difference in Harris Hip Score was observed between groups, and HHC showed comparable complication rates, supporting it as a valid alternative.
Validation· Clinical follow-up with radiographs and Harris Hip Score at mid-term (40 months).

Method· A retrospective review of 52 hips in 43 patients with mean follow-up of 7.6 years, evaluating radiographic osseointegration, bone remodeling, Harris Hip Score, and metal ion levels.
